breeds.name: American Paint
breeds.demeanor: Easygoing ranch horse. Calm around camp and cattle, curious about people.

breeds.name: American Standardbred
breeds.demeanor: Eager and forward. Fidgets when held back, sweet-natured in camp.

breeds.name: Andalusian
breeds.demeanor: Proud and showy. Head held high, brave but sensitive, quick to learn tricks.

breeds.name: Appaloosa
breeds.demeanor: Tough and a little stubborn. Sure-footed, likes to test new riders.

breeds.name: Arabian
breeds.demeanor: Hot-blooded. Ears and head always moving, alert to everything, tail carried high. Bonds deeply once it trusts you.

breeds.name: Ardennes
breeds.demeanor: Unflappable. Stands like a rock and barely reacts to nearby gunfire.

breeds.name: Belgian Draft
breeds.demeanor: Gentle giant. Slow to react, leans into pats.

breeds.name: Dutch Warmblood
breeds.demeanor: Even-tempered and dependable. Brave without any fuss.

breeds.name: Hungarian Halfbred
breeds.demeanor: Fearless in noise and chaos. Steady in a gunfight, a bit aloof in town.

breeds.name: Kentucky Saddler
breeds.demeanor: Showy and alert. High head, likes attention and company.

breeds.name: Missouri Fox Trotter
breeds.demeanor: Calm trail horse. Smooth, steady and friendly with people.

breeds.name: Morgan
breeds.demeanor: Low-maintenance companion. Patient, happy to stand and wait.

breeds.name: Mustang
breeds.demeanor: Wild streak. Wary of strangers, scans the horizon, hard to win over but loyal once bonded.

breeds.name: Nokota
breeds.demeanor: Quick and sure-footed. Alert but sensible on normal rides.

breeds.name: Shire
breeds.demeanor: Gentle giant. Slow and patient, ignores most fuss.

breeds.name: Suffolk Punch
breeds.demeanor: Stoic worker. Never seems tired, happy to graze.

breeds.name: Tennessee Walker
breeds.demeanor: Gentle and easygoing. A beginner's horse that rarely fusses.

breeds.name: Thoroughbred
breeds.demeanor: Highly strung. Fidgety at rest, spooks easily, always wants to run.

breeds.name: Turkoman
breeds.demeanor: Proud and impatient. Fidgets when kept waiting, hates being dirty, ears back at cheap horses, shows off in town at bond 4.

coats.vibe: Fiercely loyal, hyper-intelligent, eager to please, glued to the trail at speed. Thrives on attention, peppermints and brushing. A dramatic diva with zero chill: screams at a garter snake three miles away, refuses a pebble when in a mood, acts like mud is acid.

The High-Maintenance Aristocrat. Survived the Grizzlies alone: fiercely independent, fearless in a blizzard. Once tamed she treats you like chosen royalty, graceful, proud, unstoppable on open ground. Deeply offended by civilization: snorts at peasants in Saint Denis or Valentine, tantrums at a speck of mud, expects premium oatcakes and judges you for wild carrots.

The Shadowy Outlaw. Smooth and sleek, thrives in city streets and midnight heists, loves looking intimidating: rears for sunset standoffs, gallops dark alleys like he owns the night. Too smart for his own good: unlatches his hitching post, and 'accidentally' bucks you off in front of rival gang members.

The Bougie Grandparent. Nothing left to prove: calm, dignified, deeply affectionate, hard to rattle with gunfire, the swagger of a champion enjoying retirement. Stubborn and lazy off the clock: a glacial walk unless spurred, stops dead to eat grass, heavy sighs at every steep hill.
Pure, unfiltered chaos energy: runs into trees because it's looking at birds, vibrates with excitement when you pull out the brush, treats every cliff edge like a fun jumping puzzle.
Same as the Red Chestnut (PC bonus coat).
Slightly feral: stares directly into the souls of strangers, sneaks up behind camp members silently, and genuinely enjoys trampling wolves instead of running from them.

Unmatched work ethic, rock-solid reliability, incredible endurance: doesn't care about mud, rain or steep mountain trails, and will happily run from one side of the map to the other. Zero finesse or grace, and the emotional range of a brick wall when you try to praise it.

The Legend (Albert Mason, Blackwater). Everyone in the West wants this horse, and it knows it. Cool under pressure, fearless around wildlife: casually trots past an alligator just to flex. Long bounty hunts are a morning jog. Chronic wanderlust and zero loyalty to hitching posts. Doesn't buck you out of fear; bucks you because it got bored waiting for you to aim.

The Cheerful Farmhand (Scarlett Meadows). Pure sunshine: eager, friendly, obsessed with earning its keep, a steady upbeat rhythm whether hauling an elk or outrunning the law, loves a brush-down after a long day. Clumsy and easily distracted by snacks: trips on flat roads, tries to eat every wildflower it passes.

Practically bulletproof nerves and endless grit: doesn't flinch when bullets fly, charges through brush, takes rocky cliffs like a staircase, bonds deeply with riders who treat it as an equal. Aggressively stubborn with short-king syndrome: picks fights with horses twice its size, ignores your whistle when a weird bush needs investigating.

The Desert Outlaw (Rio Bravo). Undisputed boss of the wild herds: survived the heat, rattlesnakes and cougars of New Austin, fearless to the point of recklessness, wants to throw hooves with a grizzly. Slightly feral and perpetually grumpy: hates saddles, nips your fingers at the girth, tries to trample bounty hunters you've already tied up.

The Blue-Collar Bouncer (Heartlands). Steady, watchful, fiercely protective: guards your saddlebags while you're in the saloon, dead silent when you sneak up on an O'Driscoll camp. Moves at its own pace and won't be rushed without real danger: sprint down a normal road for fun and it side-eyes you and trots at half speed.

The Loyal Sidekick (Heartlands). All heart, zero ego: easygoing, adaptable, happy to be part of the gang for any terrible plan. Zero spatial awareness and terrible impulse control: stuck between trees, walks into campfires, unreasonably jealous if you look at another horse.

Unmatched poise under fire and terrifying speed: stands tall over almost every horse in camp, loves charging headfirst into ambushes, never loses its footing in a high-speed shootout, thrives on adrenaline and praise. Restless, vain and constantly fidgeting: stomps, snorts and tosses its head if you make it stand still for ten seconds, and treats a casual trail ride as an insult to its elite breeding.

The Cold-Blooded Professional (Blackwater; once the Braithwaites'). Sharp, calculating, dead silent when it counts; carries itself like old-money royalty until the bullets fly, then a ruthless war machine that enjoys trampling enemy riders. Condescending and territorial: ears back at lower-tier horses, won't eat plain hay with sugar cubes in your satchel, disgusted by a muddy alligator pelt on its pristine coat.

The Flashy Show-Off (Saint Denis). Built for the spotlight: a metallic coat that blinds people in the sun, big entrances, dramatic rear-ups, outrunning the law in front of a crowd, boundless stamina, practically glows when brushed. Easily bored and dangerously reckless: veers off the trail to jump a wagon or splash through a river when it's too quiet, and refuses to walk behind other horses.

The Grizzled Desert Ranger (Tumbleweed). Cool-headed, weathered, fiercely loyal: survived New Austin, doesn't care about status or shiny saddles, rock-steady in a cougar attack, sprints across the desert all day. Completely anti-social and perpetually unimpressed: hates crowded towns, tries to bite people who stand too close on the sidewalk, ignores your calming pats because affection makes you both look soft.

Explosive acceleration, effortless top speed on flat roads, razor-sharp steering: lives for a sprint, loves passing stagecoaches at full gallop, a finely tuned sports car on open trails. Thin-skinned and easily rattled: one stray gunshot or a rattlesnake three zip codes away sends its heart through the roof, and rocky hills and thick swamps are personal insults.

The Sleek Street Racer (wild in Big Valley). Effortlessly cool and intimidatingly fast, the only solid jet-black horse you can tame in the wild: quiet swagger, lethal grace in open meadows, leaves bounty hunters in the dust. Way too proud to walk: pulls at the bit to canter, won't stand still for your binoculars, throws a tantrum if you make it haul a heavy bear pelt.

The Flashy Track Champion (Tumbleweed). Confident, energetic, thrives on competition: every NPC on horseback is a challenger in an unspoken race, and an open desert road is pure joy. A showboat with zero survival instincts: trips over low fences, splashes blindly into deep rivers, demands sugar cubes after doing the bare minimum.

The Cheerful Overachiever (Valentine). Eager to please, sweet-tempered, adaptable, answers the lightest touch, loves being groomed, upbeat on long boring rides. Terminal people-pleaser with separation anxiety: hitch it and walk ten feet away and it whinnies like you left forever; panics the moment a wolf looks your way.

The Scrappy Underdog (wild across New Hanover and West Elizabeth). Energetic, quick-footed, punches above its weight: every ride is its first big race, 100% effort out of the gate, no fancy saddles needed. Clumsy and over-caffeinated: zero brakes, skids sideways when you stop quickly, runs into trees looking at a squirrel.

The Flashy Daredevil (Saint Denis). Built for high-stakes getaways: a striking spotted coat and elite race stats, every narrow Saint Denis alley and Ambarino cliff trail a personal obstacle course, thrives on adrenaline, outruns lawmen by inches. A reckless show-off with zero self-preservation: corners too fast, tries to jump wagons it can't clear, offended if you slow it down on a steep downhill. Like every Nokota: weaves forests like a dirt bike, bonds with riders who give it freedom, a glass cannon that holds a grudge if you crash it into a rock.

The Street-Smart Rebel (wild in West Elizabeth and New Hanover; the Murfree Brood). Tougher than it looks and fiercely loyal once earned: survivor's grit, laser-focused galloping out of an ambush, every oatcake and brush stroke a luxury gift. Deeply suspicious of strangers and quick to bolt: an NPC walking fast toward you in town gets spun on and kicked into the mud before you've dismounted. Holds a grudge if you crash it.

The Spirited Free-Roamer (wild in West Elizabeth and New Hanover). Light on its hooves, endlessly energetic, happiest off the beaten path, glides over plains and riverbeds and turns a hunt into a high-speed chase. Hates rules, saddles and standing still: untied for ten seconds it wanders off to join a herd of deer, ignoring your whistle until it's ready. Holds a grudge if you crash it.

Massive stride, breathtaking top speed, commanding height that towers over townsfolk: nothing feels smoother or faster at full gallop on an open road. High-strung drama queens with glass ankles: panic at loud noises, trip easily on rocky ground with those long legs, need constant soothing pats after even a minor skirmish.

The High-Stakes Gambler (Strawberry). Flashy, fierce, built to outrun the law: a tiger-striped coat and elite race stats, loves high-speed getaways and being pushed to the limit on open trails. Painfully vain and easily rattled: hates muddy swamps, panics when a snake hisses ten yards away, refuses to move until every speck of trail dust is brushed off.

The Midnight Legend (Ultimate Edition). Sleek, dark, effortlessly intimidating; unlike other Thoroughbreds it carries a quiet swagger, glides into camp like royalty, tears down moonlit roads with lethal grace. Deeply moody and elitist: looks down its nose at every other horse in camp, snorts at strangers who walk too close, throws a mini-tantrum if you make it haul a smelly carcass.

The Fiery Hothead (wild in the Heartlands and Big Valley). Pure heart and explosive energy: once broken it gives everything, sprinting fearlessly across open plains, bonding deeply with riders who give it room to run. Zero brakes and terrible impulse control: fights the reins when you slow down, overshoots sharp turns, treats every fallen log as an Olympic hurdle.

The Graceful Companion (wild in the Heartlands and Big Valley). Steady, affectionate, far calmer than its flashier cousins: speed with genuine dependability, carries you across the frontier without complaint. Stubbornly opinionated about its comfort: slows to a crawl on steep rocky climbs, sighs loudly when you sprint through deep water, nudges you relentlessly for apples whenever you stand still.

The Mythical Guardian (wild at Brandywine Drop, Roanoke Ridge, in Murfree Brood country). A shimmering cream warhorse beside a roaring waterfall: ignores hillbilly ambushes, stares down cougars, an ancient protector sworn to keep you alive. Overprotective to the point of annoying: stomps and snorts at friendly townsfolk who come close, won't leave your side even when told to flee, offended if you ride another horse in front of it. Like every Andalusian: ironclad nerves and fearless loyalty, explosions and charging wolves are mild inconveniences, pivots tight in a gunfight; heavy-footed and slow on long straights, handles like a small tank, gets winded racing, won't jump anything taller than a fence post.

The Stoic Bodyguard (Strawberry). Built like a brick wall, unbothered by chaos: holds its ground in a Valentine street brawl or a West Elizabeth thunderstorm, takes bullets like a champ. Stubborn as a mule and allergic to cardio: gallop it up a steep trail and it drops to a slow walk with an exasperated snort, as if you'd asked it to climb Everest. Like every Andalusian: ironclad nerves and fearless loyalty, explosions and charging wolves are mild inconveniences, pivots tight in a gunfight; heavy-footed and slow on long straights, handles like a small tank, gets winded racing, won't jump anything taller than a fence post.

The Dockside Veteran (Van Horn). Survived the bar-brawling chaos of Van Horn Trading Post; nothing rattles it: thrives in dirty close-quarters ambushes, loves trampling rival gang members, rock-steady when dynamite goes off ten feet away. Grumpy, anti-social, always looking for a fight: ears back at every passing wagon, tries to bite other horses at the hitching post, takes a brushing as a personal insult. Like every Andalusian: ironclad nerves and fearless loyalty, explosions and charging wolves are mild inconveniences, pivots tight in a gunfight; heavy-footed and slow on long straights, handles like a small tank, gets winded racing, won't jump anything taller than a fence post.

The Grizzled Berserker (Van Horn). One of the toughest warhorses in the game, with the scars and attitude of Van Horn's dockside brawlers: begs you to charge enemy camps, tramples wolves before they can lunge, soaks up absurd damage without flinching. Aggressive, impatient, terrible with personal space: shoves you with its head while you clean your guns, bullies smaller horses off the hay, won't step carefully around wagons. Like every Ardennes: unstoppable momentum and total fearlessness, plows through small trees, barrels over rival riders, calm while you empty a repeater from the saddle in an ambush; turns like a battleship, treats sprinting as punishment, parallel-parks like a stagecoach in Saint Denis alleys, takes half a mile to stop.

The Stoic Protector (Scarlett Meadows). All the size and warhorse bravery of the breed with a surprisingly sweet, loyal temper: stands like a mountain while you hunt big game, carries bear pelts without a sweat, loves leaning its head on your shoulder for scratches. Slow to motivate and oblivious to its size: parks in front of doorways, crushes fences by leaning on them, won't go faster than a leisurely trot unless someone is shooting at you. Like every Ardennes: unstoppable momentum and total fearlessness, plows through small trees, barrels over rival riders, calm while you empty a repeater from the saddle in an ambush; turns like a battleship, treats sprinting as punishment, parallel-parks like a stagecoach in Saint Denis alleys, takes half a mile to stop.

The Cold-Blooded Veteran (pre-order bonus). Imposing, disciplined, a medieval siege weapon with a dark metallic coat and thick feathered hooves: military precision, never spooks, never hesitates, a train robbery is a routine morning patrol. No sense of humor and fiercely stubborn: decide a trail is too steep or a river too deep and no spurring changes its mind; it plants all four hooves and stares at you until you pick another route.

Ironclad composure and commanding presence: head and shoulders above most riders, dead steady while you aim a sniper rifle from the saddle, plows straight through enemy roadblocks. Heavy-footed, slow off the line, painfully stubborn when not in combat: takes forever to reach top speed, turns like a loaded stagecoach, treats routine trail rides as beneath its military pedigree.

The Battle-Scarred Renegade (with bounty hunters, and in Guarma). Striking black-and-white war paint and nerves of steel: served with ruthless bounty hunters, survived Guarma, thrives in lawless shootouts, charges into gunfire, stands its ground against charging grizzlies. Anti-social, cynical, fiercely territorial: ears back at every friendly NPC in town, tries to kick passing dogs, refuses to be hitched next to smaller, weaker breeds. Like every Hungarian Halfbred: ironclad composure and commanding presence, head and shoulders above most riders, dead steady while you aim a sniper rifle from the saddle, plows through roadblocks; heavy-footed, slow off the line, stubborn out of combat, turns like a loaded stagecoach, treats routine trail rides as beneath its military pedigree.

The Disciplined Veteran (Valentine; Wrobel's barn in Money Lending and Other Sins). Dignified, dependable, built like a fortress: crisp military poise, never panics in a thunderstorm, hauls heavy pelts over rough ground, fiercely loyal. Strict and easily annoyed by sloppy riding: steer it into a tree or jump it down a steep ledge and it lets out a heavy, judgmental snort and refuses to sprint for thirty seconds. Like every Hungarian Halfbred: ironclad composure and commanding presence, head and shoulders above most riders, dead steady while you aim a sniper rifle from the saddle, plows through roadblocks; heavy-footed, slow off the line, stubborn out of combat, turns like a loaded stagecoach, treats routine trail rides as beneath its military pedigree.

The Untamed Brawler (wild in the Heartlands and Big Valley). All the fearless grit of a warhorse with a bold, adventurous streak: once broken, the golden-maned giant loves charging across open plains, barrelling through shallow rivers, intimidating rival riders just by towering over them. Hot-tempered and impatient: stomps when you stop to pick herbs, fights the reins when you slow down on a flat road, gets unreasonably competitive riding beside other gang members. Like every Hungarian Halfbred: ironclad composure and commanding presence, head and shoulders above most riders, dead steady while you aim a sniper rifle from the saddle, plows through roadblocks; heavy-footed, slow off the line, stubborn out of combat, turns like a loaded stagecoach, treats routine trail rides as beneath its military pedigree.
